## Environment

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(rtauargus) #We want 1.3.6

data("indiv_dt")
indiv_dt[82, "TURNOVER"] <- 40000 #We create some dominance
data("nuts23_fr_corr_table")
data("activity_corr_table")

options(scipen = 999)
loc_tauargus <- "Y:/Logiciels/TauArgus/TauArgus4.2.3/TauArgus.exe"
options(rtauargus.tauargus_exe = loc_tauargus)
```

## Tabulating fit-for-rtauargus data from microdata

`tabulate_micro_data()` function computes tabular data from microdata and various additional variables to assess primary secrecy.

```{r}
TURN_act88_size <- tabulate_micro_data(
  df = indiv_dt,
  cat_var = c("A88", "SIZE"),
  pond_var = "WEIGHT",
  resp_var = "TURNOVER",
  marge_label = "Total"
)
head(TURN_act88_size)
```

This can be industrialised for multiple response variables and with hierarchies. Hierarchies are variables that are nested one in the other and therefore should be addressed as a single variable when protected.

```{r}
TURN_PROD_act_size <- tabulate_micro_data(
  df = indiv_dt,
  cat_var = c("SIZE"),
  hrc_vars = list(
    ACTIVITY = c("A10","A21")
  ),
  pond_var = "WEIGHT",
  resp_var = c("TURNOVER","PRODUCTION"),
  marge_label = "Total"
)

head(TURN_PROD_act_size)
```

## Prepping the data: rounding and primary secret computation

$\tau$-Argus doesn't accept decimals in frequencies and too many decimals in value may cause unstable results in $\tau$-Argus. We compute rounded variables to run the program. Not rounded variables remain in the tableand may be used for dissemination along with the SDC status that will be computed.

We also would like to keep track of the rules we apply (frequency and dominance).

```{r}
prepping <- function(df){
  df |>  mutate(
    dom = TURNOVER_max/TURNOVER_tot,
    is_secret_freq = nb_obs > 0 & nb_obs < 3,
    is_secret_dom = (TURNOVER_max > 0.85*TURNOVER_tot),
    FREQ = round(nb_obs,0),
    VALUE = round(TURNOVER_tot,5) 
  ) |>
    mutate(
      is_secret_prim = is_secret_freq | is_secret_dom
    )
}

TURN_act88_size <- TURN_act88_size |>
  prepping()

TURN_act88_size |> count(is_secret_prim)
```

## Single table protection

`tab_rtauargus()` protects a single table. The SDC status is available in a variable named `Status` and coded B, D, V as in stand-alone $\tau$-Argus outputs.

```{r}
TURN_act88_size <- tab_rtauargus(
  tabular=TURN_act88_size,
  dir_name = "tauargus_files/",
  files_name = "TURN_act88_size",
  explanatory_vars = c("A88","SIZE"),
  secret_var = "is_secret_prim",
  value = "VALUE",
  freq = "FREQ",
  totcode = c(A88="Total",SIZE="Total"),
  verbose = FALSE
)
```

## Hierarchies

### Building .hrc files

Now we want to protect TURNOVER x {A10,A21,size}

We see A10 and A21 as different levels of a same hierarchy.

A hierarchy may be represented as a tree, each level being a branch and last level are leaves. There may be as many levels as needed. A primary secret on a leaf must be protected with a secondary suppression on another leaf from the same branch (or on the branch total, depending on the circumstances)

$\tau$-argus uses specific .hrc files to treat hierarchies.

We first need to produce the .hrc file. It can be done with `write_hrc2()`from any data.frame with one variable for each level of the hierarchy.

```{r}
hrc_act <- write_hrc2(activity_corr_table |> select(A10,A21) |> distinct(),
                      file_name="tauargus_files/hrc/hrc_act.hrc")
file.edit(hrc_act)
```

Let's build other hierarchies to be used later. The data.frame may be a correspondance table that you have, describing all theoritical cases, or it may be constructed from the microdata:

```{r}
#From a correspondance table
hrc_nuts <- write_hrc2(nuts23_fr_corr_table |> 
                         distinct(),
                       file_name="tauargus_files/hrc/hrc_nuts.hrc")

#From the microdata indiv_dt
hrc_act2 <- write_hrc2(
  indiv_dt |> 
    select(A10,A21,A88) |> 
    arrange(A10,A21,A88) |> 
    distinct(),
  file_name="tauargus_files/hrc/hrc_act2_md.hrc")
```

### Single table protection with .hrc

We can now protect our hierarchical table. Let's run it first without `hrc` : primary suppression in ACTIVITY=="I" leads to secondary suppression in E (lowest value, so it was the best candidate considering the parameters).

```{r}
TURN_PROD_act_size <- TURN_PROD_act_size |>
  prepping()

head(TURN_PROD_act_size)

TURN_PROD_act_size_hrcunprotected <- tab_rtauargus(
  TURN_PROD_act_size,
  dir_name = "tauargus_files/",
  files_name = "TURN_act_size",
  explanatory_vars = c("ACTIVITY","SIZE"),
  secret_var = "is_secret_prim",
  value = "VALUE",
  freq = "FREQ",
  totcode = c(ACTIVITY="Total",SIZE="Total"),
  verbose = FALSE
)
TURN_PROD_act_size_hrcunprotected |> filter(Status != "V") |> kable()

```

Now with the use of the hrc parameter, primary suppression in ACTIVITY=="I" leads to secondary suppression in H because H and I both belong to aggregate ACTIVITY=="GI":

```{r}

TURN_PROD_act_size_hrcprotected <- tab_rtauargus(
  TURN_PROD_act_size,
  dir_name = "tauargus_files/",
  files_name = "TURN_act_size",
  explanatory_vars = c("ACTIVITY","SIZE"),
  hrc = c(ACTIVITY = hrc_act),
  secret_var = "is_secret_prim",
  value = "VALUE",
  freq = "FREQ",
  totcode = c(ACTIVITY="Total",SIZE="Total"),
  verbose = FALSE
)

TURN_PROD_act_size_hrcprotected |> filter(Status != "V") |> kable()

```

## Linked tables

### General case

I would like to protect the following tables :

- TURNOVER x {a10,a21,a88,size} = TURNOVER x {ACTIVITY,SIZE}

<!-- -->

- TURNOVER x {a10,a21,a88,size,type} = TURNOVER x {ACTIVITY,SIZE,TYPE}

- TURNOVER x {a10,a21,a88,nuts2,nuts3} = TURNOVER x {ACTIVITY,NUTS}

Let's compute the tables from microdata:

```{r}
TURN_act_size <- tabulate_micro_data(
  df = indiv_dt,
  cat_var = c("SIZE"),
  hrc_vars = list(
    ACTIVITY = c("A10","A21","A88")
  ),
  pond_var = "WEIGHT",
  resp_var = "TURNOVER",
  marge_label = "Total"
) 

TURN_act_size_type <- tabulate_micro_data(
  df = indiv_dt,
  cat_var = c("SIZE","TYPE"),
  hrc_vars = list(
    ACTIVITY = c("A10","A21","A88")
  ),
  pond_var = "WEIGHT",
  resp_var = "TURNOVER",
  marge_label = "Total"
) 

TURN_act_nuts <- tabulate_micro_data(
  df = indiv_dt,
  hrc_vars = list(
    ACTIVITY = c("A10","A21","A88"),
    NUTS = c("NUTS2","NUTS3")
  ),
  pond_var = "WEIGHT",
  resp_var = "TURNOVER",
  marge_label = "Total"
)
```

To protect multiple tables at once, we need to work with named lists. The list of tables may be as long as needed (many hundreds tables in a single `tab_multi_manager()` call). Other parameters also work using named lists:

```{r}
#Tables
list_tab <- list(
  TURN_act_size = TURN_act_size,
  TURN_act_size_type = TURN_act_size_type,
  TURN_act_nuts = TURN_act_nuts
) |> 
  lapply(prepping)

#Explanatory variables
list_expl <- list(
  TURN_act_size = c("ACTIVITY","SIZE"),
  TURN_act_size_type = c("ACTIVITY","SIZE","TYPE"),
  TURN_act_nuts = c("ACTIVITY","NUTS")
)

#Total codes
total_codes <- "Total"

#HRC files
list_hrc <- list(
  ACTIVITY = hrc_act2,
  NUTS = hrc_nuts
)
```

Then we call `tab_multi_manager()`. This function calls `tab_rtauargus()`as many times as needed, and most often than not calls it multiple times on each table until all common cells are protected consistently. It returns a list of data.frame, each containing the original data + secrecy variables named `is_secret_x`, with $x$ ranging from 1 to the number of the last iteration. This is the last `is_secret_prim` that contains the final secrecy status.

A journal reports on all the process and a summary of secrecy per table.

```{r}
res <- tab_multi_manager(
  list_tables = list_tab,
  list_explanatory_vars = list_expl,
  dir_name = "tauargus_files/multi",
  hrc = list_hrc,
  totcode = total_codes,
  value = "VALUE",
  freq = "FREQ",
  secret_var = "is_secret_prim"
)
file.edit("tauargus_files/multi/journal.txt")
head(res$TURN_act_size)
```

### Unnested hierarchies

We create A20 by regrouping B, G and I. A20 still belongs to *some* ACTIVITY hierarchy, but is not nested in A10 because of B not being in GI (GI contains G, H, I). Thus we cannot use `hrc_act`to treat a table with BGI. We compute a new table and a new hierarchy:

```{r}
TURN_actBGI_size <- tabulate_micro_data(
  df = indiv_dt |> mutate(A20 = if_else(A21 %in% c("B","G","I"), "BGI",A21)),
  cat_var = c("SIZE"),
  hrc_vars = list(
    ACTIVITY = c("A20")
  ),
  pond_var = "WEIGHT",
  resp_var = "TURNOVER",
  marge_label = "Total"
) |> 
  prepping()

hrc_actBGI <- write_hrc2(activity_corr_table |> mutate(A20 = if_else(A21 %in% c("B","G","I"), "BGI",A21)) |> select(A20) |> distinct(),
                         file_name="tauargus_files/hrc/hrc_actBI.hrc")
```

We will add them to the bundle of tables we are already treating together. We need to re-run `tab_multi_manager()`each time the tables change, since tables are linked by margins and primary secret on one may lead to secondary secret on the others.

We use the parameter `alt_hrc` to parameter a different hierarchy for TURN_actBGI_size.

```{r}
list_tabBGI <- list_tab |> append(list(TURN_actBGI_size = TURN_actBGI_size))
list_explBGI <- list_expl |> append(list(TURN_actBGI_size = c("ACTIVITY","SIZE")))
list_alt_hrc <- list(
  TURN_actBGI_size = c(ACTIVITY = hrc_actBGI)
)

resBGI <- tab_multi_manager(
  list_tables = list_tabBGI,
  list_explanatory_vars = list_explBGI,
  dir_name = "tauargus_files/multi_BGI",
  hrc = list_hrc,
  alt_hrc = list_alt_hrc,
  totcode = total_codes,
  value = "VALUE",
  freq = "FREQ",
  secret_var = "is_secret_prim"
) |> 
  imap( ~ {
    .x %>%
      rename(is_secret_final = ncol(.x)) 
  })

file.edit("tauargus_files/multi_BGI/journal.txt")
```

### Other options

There are many options available to custom your `tab_multi_manager()`call. We'll see three.

#### Protection interval and secrecy summary

Default protection interval is a +-10%. We do not encourage to change it but you may need to, depending on your own SDC policy or some limitations (it may occur that $\tau$-argus cannot find a proper protection pattern with a 10% protection interval for instance): `ip_start`.

Although you already have a secrecy summary in the journal.txt, using `summary_secret` adds to the returned list a list of data.frame with a summary for each table treated.

```{r}
res_ip <- tab_multi_manager(
  list_tables = list_tab,
  list_explanatory_vars = list_expl,
  dir_name = "tauargus_files/multi_ip",
  hrc = list_hrc,
  totcode = total_codes,
  value = "VALUE",
  freq = "FREQ",
  secret_var = "is_secret_prim",
  ip_start = 2,
  summary_secret=TRUE
)

file.edit("tauargus_files/multi_ip/journal.txt")
file.edit("tauargus_files/multi/journal.txt")
```

#### Alternative total

We may have a table computed only on some activities. The total of this table is not the supertotal "Total" but the group "BE" for ACTIVITY. We can handle this with `alt_totcode`.

```{r}
#New table
TURN_actBE_size_type <- tabulate_micro_data(
  df = indiv_dt |> filter(A10=="BE"),
  cat_var = c("SIZE","TYPE"),
  hrc_vars = list(
    ACTIVITY = c("A10","A21","A88")
  ),
  pond_var = "WEIGHT",
  resp_var = "TURNOVER",
  marge_label = "Total"
) |> filter(ACTIVITY != "Total")

#Building the lists for treatment
list_tab <- list(
  TURN_act_size = TURN_act_size,
  TURN_actBE_size_type = TURN_actBE_size_type,
  TURN_act_nuts = TURN_act_nuts
) |> 
  lapply(prepping)

list_expl <- list(
  TURN_act_size = c("ACTIVITY","SIZE"),
  TURN_actBE_size_type = c("ACTIVITY","SIZE","TYPE"),
  TURN_act_nuts = c("ACTIVITY","NUTS")
)

hrc_act2 <- write_hrc2(activity_corr_table |> 
                         mutate(A88 = sub("^0+", "", A88)) |> 
                         distinct(),
                       file_name="tauargus_files/hrc/hrc_act2.hrc")

list_hrc <- list(
  ACTIVITY = hrc_act2,
  NUTS = hrc_nuts
)

#Running with alt_totcode
res_alttot <- tab_multi_manager(
  list_tables = list_tab,
  list_explanatory_vars = list_expl,
  dir_name = "tauargus_files/multi_alttot",
  hrc = list_hrc,
  totcode = total_codes,
  alt_totcode = list(
    TURN_actBE_size_type = c(ACTIVITY = "BE")
  ),
  value = "VALUE",
  freq = "FREQ",
  secret_var = "is_secret_prim",
  summary_secret=TRUE
)
```
